algorithm.Title: Postpartum - Urination Pain - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Postpartum painful urination assessment, combining NHS.UK's C-section recovery urinary-symptom warning with the cystitis guidance already used for Urination Pain - Female (batch14).
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 now. Do not let the patient drive. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is pain in the side or back below the ribs the primary concern rather than pain during urination?
questions.Information: Primary side or back pain below the ribs belongs in the Flank Pain pathway.

questions.Question: Along with urinary symptoms, is there confusion, trouble breathing or very fast breathing, fainting, cold or clammy skin, or rapidly worsening severe illness?
questions.Information: These are sepsis red flags, and postpartum infection can progress quickly - always treated as an emergency.

questions.Question: Is there pain when urinating, leaking urine, back or flank pain, fever, or blood in the urine?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance lists painful or leaking urination after a C-section as needing prompt review, and the same applies to any postpartum delivery given the shared infection risk.

advice.Title: Emergency postpartum infection precautions
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 now. Do not let the patient drive. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening confusion; worsening breathing.

advice.Title: Urgent postpartum urinary symptom review
Content: Arrange prompt clinical assessment; the exact non-emergency Qatar destination remains GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED. Postpartum urinary symptoms may need examination and testing.
Call Back If: fever develops; back pain worsens.

references: NHS.UK, "Caesarean section - Recovery" (urinary symptom warning), https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/caesarean-section/recovery/ (page last reviewed 04 January 2023)
NHS.UK, "Cystitis" (already cited for Urination Pain - Female, batch14), https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cystitis/
